record.summary: A 7-10 story mid-rise student/faculty housing building at 525 Nelson Rising Lane, one of four connected buildings (with Hearst Tower, the West and South buildings) in UCSF's Mission Bay housing complex, built together and opened together around 2005.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson and DataSF's Assessor tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Nelson Rising Lane alone is ~13 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.

facts.value: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) with Fisher Friedman Associates
One of four connected buildings (Hearst Tower, North Building, West Building, South Building) totaling 298,800 sq ft for 750+ residents around a shared at-grade courtyard

milestones.text: UC Regents approve a $112,816,000 budget and external financing for the Mission Bay Block 20 Housing and Retail Project -- one 15-story tower (Hearst Tower) and three mid-rise buildings, including this one, around a shared courtyard, 298,800 residential asf and 430 apartment units total -- with construction to begin June 2003 and full occupancy anticipated by October 2005

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, blocked to automated fetches with a 403); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further in this pass; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history. The same September 2008 Regents presentation (used for Byers Hall, Genentech Hall, Rock Hall and Rutter Center) includes one more photo on its "Architectural Context" slide labeled only "Housing," showing what looks like more than one building together; it wasn't used here because it can't be confidently attributed to this specific one.

2026-09-21 pass: the November 2002 Regents item covers the whole Block 20 project (one tower plus three mid-rise buildings) rather than naming this building individually; identification of this record as one of the three mid-rise buildings follows from its own facts entry, not a direct name match in the Regents record.

record.notes: Part of a single UCSF Mission Bay student/faculty housing complex (Hearst Tower plus North, West and South/Student Housing buildings) built together in Mission Bay's first development phase and opened together around 2005 -- four connected buildings totaling 298,800 sq ft for 750+ residents, surrounding a shared at-grade courtyard, per UCSF's own housing-office description. Architect Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) with Fisher Friedman Associates. This building: the North Building, 525 Nelson Rising Lane, a 7-10 story mid-rise.
